Subject: Telemetry governance & export model for private VPC deployment

Hi Ken —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As we start scoping the private VPC deployment for Globex, one of the key items we want to lock down early is the telemetry & observability model so we can align on security, data residency, and operational expectations. I want to capture a short set of questions and propose a first-pass approach so we can converge quickly.

Quick asks from our side:
- Do you have a preferred SIEM (we heard Splunk HEC is in use) and an internal endpoint(s) we should target for the PoC?
- Retention constraints: what minimum retention windows and export policies are required by compliance?
- PII/PCI masking rules: are there fields that must be redacted before any egress?
- Network constraints: will egress to a managed collector be allowed from a dedicated outbound NAT, or must we use an on-prem forwarder inside their network?

Suggested model (high level):
1) Sidecar/forwarder pattern inside the customer VPC (recommended) — provides locality and control, supports TLS mTLS to their SIEM, and lets us apply customer-specific scrubbing rules before egress.
2) OpenTelemetry for tracing and logs in JSON/OTLP where possible; metrics via Prometheus remote_write to their metrics backend or a metrics proxy.
3) Strong auth: mTLS + short-lived tokens produced by their gateway or a mutual-auth proxy. No plaintext credentials in config.
4) Sampling and aggregation: we will propose default sampling rules (10% traces for high-volume routes) and rollouts so production cost is controlled while preserving signal.

Attachments: draft checklist and proposal (we'll circulate a formal PDF once we have answers).

If you can answer the above by EOD Fri we can deliver a tailored PoC plan and a proposed network diagram next week.

Best,
Laura

Laura — thanks for putting this together. A few quick answers and follow-ups from Globex Security/Ops: 

1) SIEM: we operate Splunk Enterprise, preferred ingestion is HEC with token auth. We can expose an internal HEC endpoint reachable from your forwarder.
2) Retention: sensitive logs must be retained internally for 7 years per our compliance; aggregated telemetry retained for 30 days in the vendor tier. We need guarantees that raw payloads containing account identifiers never leave our custody unmasked.
3) PII/PCI: any PAN/SSN/Account numbers must be redacted at the source. We can provide a regex set and sample records.
4) Network: For security approvals, egress must originate from a customer-controlled bastion/NAT and be restricted to specific IPs. We prefer a forwarder inside our VPC that does final TLS termination to our Splunk HEC.

PoC ask: Can you produce a minimal configuration that runs in a test VPC and forwards to our HEC? We'd like to see TLS handshake details and auth flow. Also: what visibility will Redwood provide into per-route sampling and token usage?

I'll loop in our Ops alias to coordinate HEC endpoint provisioning.

—Ken

Ken / team —

Appreciate the details — below are concrete technical options and the tradeoffs so we can pick a path for the PoC. I'll attach a short proposal PDF with diagrams.

Option A — In-VPC forwarder (recommended):
- Deploy a small VM (or container) in your VPC that runs our forwarder. Forwarder receives OTLP/JSON, applies configured scrub rules, and forwards to your internal Splunk HEC endpoint over mTLS.
- Auth: mTLS between forwarder and HEC. Forwarder uses ephemeral certs rotated by a customer CA or a short-lived token from your gateway.
- Network: egress controlled by your NAT; firewall rule restricts to the HEC IP(s).
- Pros: Minimal cross-network trust, full control for Globex, easiest for compliance signoff.
- Cons: Customer owns availability of forwarder (we can offer monitoring playbooks).

Option B — Enclave sidecar + Redundant collector:
- Deploy our lightweight sidecar next to model serving nodes that forwards to a local collector. Collector performs heavy scrubbing and batching before sending to HEC.
- Pros: Reduces traffic spikes to HEC, better per-service correlation, allows route-level sampling.
- Cons: More components to operate.

Format & tooling notes:
- Logs/traces: OTLP (protobuf/HTTP) preferred. Provide correlation via trace_id/span_id in JSON and attach a stable request_id for cross-signal joins.
- Tracing hooks: instrumented libraries must set baggage fields only after redaction checks. We will provide a redaction middleware for the most common frameworks.
- Metrics: Prometheus remote_write or pushgateway to a proxy inside the VPC; Prom metrics are low-bandwidth and useful for SLO/alerting.
- Sampling: default 10% APM sample across the fleet; for error/latency spikes we auto-upgrade sampling for the affected route.
- Scrubbing: support regex-based scrubbing, field-level allow-listing, and tokenization for anything flagged as sensitive. Scrubbing policies are declarative YAML.

For the PoC we propose:
- Deliverable 1: Terraform template for a single forwarder instance + config that points to your HEC (test endpoint).
- Deliverable 2: Example agent config with scrubbing rules + sample logs showing redaction.
- Deliverable 3: Small runbook for Ops on cert rotation and troubleshooting.

Attachment: telemetry-governance-proposal-v1.pdf (diagram + sample configs). I'll also add a short checklist XLSX.

Let us know which option you prefer; we can start building the Terraform/Ansible artifacts immediately and target a PoC within two weeks.

Thanks,
Jonas
